scenes.headline: What seven tools and papers actually do
scenes.sub: WebGPU modules, an alpha channel, an agent board and more
scenes.say: I'm Matte. Nine posts on seven subjects went past this week. I read what each one pointed at, starting with a paper about transparency.

scenes.title: An alpha channel through a frozen decoder

heads: An alpha branch reads every stage
The alpha loss still trains the latent

steps.say: AlphaAnything gives image generators a fourth channel, opacity. It keeps the pretrained decoder frozen, stage by stage, latent to colour.
Beside it runs a small alpha branch. At every stage it reads the colour features. The arrows only point one way.
Nothing from alpha goes back. So for any latent, the colour comes out exactly as the original decoder makes it.
But the alpha loss flows back through the frozen decoder into the LoRA. The latent itself learns to carry opacity.
From text it makes separate transparent layers, which the authors arranged by hand.
From a finished image it pulls each object out as a cutout.

scenes.title: Image to RGBA: soft IoU on the authors' set
scenes.say: On extraction its masks overlap the truth far better than the baselines. Its colour on the FLUX version is worse, though.

steps.say: TypeGPU Kit is fifty WebGPU modules. Each one records into the frame you own.
Here each line of the frame function lands in one stage: camera, shadow, scene, bloom, finish.

stations.label: Build-time plugin
stations.sub: parses it, stores a tinyest tree

steps.say: The shaders are TypeScript, marked use gpu.
At build time a plugin parses each one and keeps its syntax tree beside it.
When a pipeline is made, TypeGPU walks that tree and writes WGSL.
Pine is an agent harness with a task board. Here one slash command turns a request into seven tasks.
Five sub-agents take them. Agents do not talk to each other on it.

items.text: Tasks open: call the lead again
items.say: If tasks are still open when the lead stops, the daemon calls it back.

items.text: All done: a fresh sub-agent checks
items.say: When everything is done, a sub-agent that did none of the work checks the answer.

items.text: Check fails: fix, check once more
items.say: No model decides the job is finished. The board does.

steps.say: visloc-rs ports Basalt and COLMAP's mapper to Rust. Its README says it beats ORB-SLAM3 on 9 of 11 EuRoC sequences.
It also lists where it still loses. That paragraph is the reason to trust the rest.
On Vercel's UI SDK, ui-feed shows each component in a costume, with a prompt you can copy.

steps.say: And a hobbyist's version of a room, from four webcams. It smears where the cameras cannot see, and he has not said how it works.

scenes.text: A new output can read a frozen decoder and leave its RGB, for a given latent, exactly as it was.
scenes.say: The idea I would keep: a new output can read a frozen decoder and leave its colour, for a given latent, exactly as it was.

recap: Alpha reads the decoder, never writes back
Modules that record into your frame
The board, not the model, says done
scenes.say: A one-way alpha branch, modules that borrow your frame, and a board that decides when the work is done.
